name: VeriTomiX
mission: A physics-based test bench for medical imaging: simulated patients and phantoms with known truth, used to show where imaging software and AI can be trusted, and where they cannot.

team.name: Sai Kiran Kumar Nalla
team.role: PhD · medical imaging, creator of CASSOULET

why.title: Imaging AI needs an answer key
why.lede: A patient scan is realistic, but nobody knows the true size or uptake of every lesion in it. Without that ground truth, an average score on a dataset cannot say when a tool stops being reliable.
why.answer: VeriTomiX designs the truth first: the lesion, the activity and the scanner are all known, so every output can be scored against the right answer. 3D-printed phantoms scanned on real scanners keep the simulation honest.

cassoulet.name: Named after the cassoulet of Toulouse, where it was built: many ingredients (masks, STL, TACs, sinograms, reconstructions) slow-cooked in one pot, a single linked session.
cassoulet.expansion: Compositional Anthropomorphic Spatial Synthesizer for ground-truth Lesion Export and Tomography
cassoulet.motto: Design known PET lesion truth. Simulate digitally. Validate physically.
cassoulet.lede: CASSOULET is the simulation engine inside VeriTomiX. It creates lesions with known geometry, activity, heterogeneity and time behaviour, and the same truth object can be tested digitally in simulated PET or physically as a 3D-printed phantom insert.

modules.name: Designer
modules.text: Lesion masks, heterogeneity maps and reusable STL truth objects.

modules.name: Modeller
modules.text: Printable inserts and geometry, plus the MuPET multiphysics route.

modules.name: Simulator
modules.text: 3D PET experiments: projection, noise and reconstruction, static or dynamic.

modules.name: Analyser
modules.text: Measures every output against the truth it came from.

physics: DICOM in: a CT gives the anatomy and the 511 keV attenuation map; PET headers give dose, timing, prompts and delays
Depth of interaction (3 × 3 sub-LORs), F-18 positron range, 0.5° photon non-collinearity and residual detector blur
Time of flight (385 ps, 29 bins on the Discovery MI), TOF single-scatter simulation and singles-product randoms
Poisson counting noise, then GPU reconstruction (OSEM, or BSREM with an edge-preserving prior) and DICOM export
Reconstruction never sees the model that made the data: it assumes simpler endpoints and a Gaussian PSF
Numerical checks: gradient and projector adjoint tests agree to about 10⁻⁹

twoTests.name: Physical phantom test
twoTests.steps: Export STL → print insert → scan phantom

cassoulet.compare: Both measured outputs are compared with the original truth: detectability, SUV recovery, segmentation, heterogeneity and radiomics.
cassoulet.session: One session map links the four modules, so every result keeps its lineage: which truth, which settings, which outputs.

mupet.text: MuPET (Multiphysics PET) combines computational mass-transport physics with image-domain PET noise modelling. It gives CASSOULET a fast image-level route for phantom and lesion studies, next to the projection-domain simulator.

figs.caption: MuPET workflow: multiphysics activity maps combined with scanner-derived noise statistics.
MuPET dynamic images of a phantom after noise addition.

cassoulet.ai: Built with AI-assisted coding for interface work and migration, with core algorithms, scientific assumptions and data handling checked by hand and through tests. The original MATLAB version was written manually.

whatsNew.title: What's new in the desktop app
whatsNew.lede: The Python rebuild now runs the whole digital test inside one Simulator workbench, with an editing toolkit for masks and a CAD workbench for printable inserts. Status: work in progress, July 2026.

items.name: One workbench, eight linked steps
items.text: Session and images, CT registration, lesion insertion, scanner and protocol, forward projection, dynamic TAC, outputs and QA, all kept in one session.

fig.caption: Simulator workbench: the linked steps, the session inputs tree and the lesion-insertion protocol panel (image views left out).

items.name: CT registration
items.text: A CT is registered onto the PET reference grid, giving the registered CT and the attenuation (μ-map) input for the projection.

items.name: Hybrid lesion insertion
items.text: Lesions from files, design masks, STL assets, modeller meshes or generated shapes; uniform, textured, speckled or spiculated patterns; activity set by SUV target, contrast or a time-activity curve; placed at the crosshair, several per image.

items.name: Forward projection and noise
items.text: Projection with attenuation, scatter, randoms and normalisation, then Poisson noise with a noise factor and seed; every intermediate sinogram can be inspected, with a bed plan for multi-bed coverage.

items.name: Reconstruction and outputs
items.text: OSEM reconstruction with iterations and subsets, run in the background on the projection bundle; outputs and QA stay attached to the session, static or frame by frame for dynamic studies.

items.name: Mask editor toolkit
items.text: Slicer-style editing on the slice views: paint, erase, spline, scissors, flood fill, shape drawing, boolean operations, grow and shrink, smoothing, split labels, crop and resample, with layers, per-layer 3D opacity and maximised views.

items.name: CAD workbench
items.text: Sketch, extrude, fillet, chamfer and boolean steps on a feature timeline, primitives and construction planes, porous lattice infill, several display modes and export to STL, STEP, OBJ or IGES.

fig.caption: Modeller test render: a sketch on the XY plane extruded into a body, with the feature timeline below.

items.name: Analyser workbench
items.text: A first Analyser window: simulation outputs and ground-truth masks as data nodes, compare and metrics tools, and generated reports. Early stage.

pipeline.title: From phantom to evaluation dataset
pipeline.lede: Every case follows the same chain, and every setting is logged, so a result can always be traced back to its cause.

steps.name: Phantom or patient model
steps.text: An anthropomorphic phantom or a virtual patient: anatomy, attenuation and background activity.

steps.name: Lesion insertion
steps.text: Lesions of known size, shape, contrast and texture are placed where they are needed.

steps.name: Scanner simulation
steps.text: A scanner model turns activity into measured data: attenuation, resolution, scatter, randoms and noise.

steps.name: Reconstruction
steps.text: The data are reconstructed with clinical-style algorithms and settings.

steps.name: Evaluation dataset
steps.text: Images, truth masks and settings are exported together, ready to score any tool.

goals.name: Evaluate AI and imaging software
goals.text: Test segmentation, detection, quantification and reconstruction tools against cases where the right answer is known, and map the conditions where they fail rather than reporting one average score.

goals.name: Create new datasets
goals.text: Build controlled, privacy-free imaging datasets with exact truth and full provenance: sizes, contrasts, count levels, scanners and reconstructions that real cohorts rarely cover.

goals.name: Physics-informed AI digital twins
goals.text: Combine the physics of the scanner and the tracer with learned models, so a digital twin of a patient or a phantom can be simulated quickly and still respect the physics.

closing: VeriTomiX is an independent research effort. It adds a controlled technical-evidence layer; it does not replace clinical validation.

scanners.title: Scanner models
scanners.lede: CASSOULET carries research models of two clinical PET/CT scanners. They are built from published specifications and NEMA data, and every assumption is written down. They are not vendor system models.
notes: Published: module and block counts, crystal sizes, ring diameter, axial field of view, energy window, timing.
Derived: crystal rows and crystals per ring from the published hierarchy.
Assumed and labelled: polygon packing, some block gaps (no public gap dimensions for the Omni), detector efficiency profile.
The CT section is drawn for context only; attenuation comes from the μ-map.

figures.caption: The abdominal phantom positioned on the Discovery MI model.

validation.title: Case studies: physical validation
validation.lede: A simulator is only useful if it is trusted. These studies put CASSOULET next to real scans of physical phantoms on both scanner models.

items.kicker: Multicentre · Discovery MI and Omni Legend
items.name: Digital twins against a printed phantom at two centres
items.lede: The same 36-insert gyroid phantom was 3D-printed and scanned at two facilities, and simulated on both scanner models. Overall recovery agreed within the ±10 % equivalence margin (TOST, α = 0.05) for both scanners.

fig.caption: Theoretical design, CASSOULET simulation, Toulouse and Rambam, on both scanner models.

more: Physical scans: IUCT Oncopole (Toulouse) and Rambam Health Care Campus (Haifa), from shared print files.
Only 14 of 27 designs stay within ±10 % for TOF TBRmax in every session; one design has a 22 % median error.
An earlier pooled analysis gave DMI ρc 0.905 (bias +1.8 %) and Omni ρc 0.925 (bias +1.3 %).
Status: manuscript in revision (31 Oct 2026).

figs.caption: Earlier pooled 27-configuration analysis: recovery, Bland–Altman agreement and TOST equivalence.
Exact configuration matching across the 27 printed geometries, per facility.

gsr.goal: Check whether one simulation per scanner reproduces a 3D-printed porous phantom scanned at two hospitals.
gsr.simulated: 36 gyroid insert designs (27 with 10–20 mm targets) on 25 cm TOF and 32 cm non-TOF models, five frames each, against four measured sessions per scanner.
gsr.results: 720 of 864 endpoint comparisons within ±10 %. Mean recovery error 4.4–5.0 %, local-contrast error 6.2–7.9 %. Background texture and some local contrasts are not yet matched.

items.name: A Siemens patient scanned again on a virtual Discovery MI

gsr.goal: Test whether a real body's anatomy and uptake survive a different, virtual scanner.
gsr.simulated: A healthy volunteer's total-body CT rebuilt as about 150 structures, organ uptake from the measured PET, 11 synthetic lesions, six DMI beds, OSEM and BSREM.
gsr.results: Organ recovery against the input 0.97–1.04 (bias −2.6 % to +3.9 %). Simulated organ SUVs within about 6 % of the measured Siemens scan; tissue texture is smoother.

fig.caption: Measured Siemens PET, activity input, OSEM-style and BSREM simulations at four body levels.

more: Source: sub-000, DEPICT-RH / Multimodal-HC dataset, CC BY 4.0 (Hinge et al.).
Uniform uptake per organ, so measured tissue texture is absent by design.

items.name: Physical vs simulated images, voxel by voxel
items.lede: Side-by-side images and line profiles of physical and simulated scans, then a direct voxel-level comparison inside matched 3D Slicer volumes of interest.
more: Mean recovery agrees well; voxel-level agreement is moderate (peak-voxel Lin's ρc 0.523, R² 0.689), as expected from different noise textures.
Intra-VOI heterogeneity and noise follow the physical trend; Bland–Altman bias on peak voxels is small.
Status: research result; part of the multicentre analysis.

figs.caption: Voxel-level VOI validation: Slicer VOIs, peak-voxel correlation, voxel distributions and Bland–Altman agreement.

items.kicker: NEMA IEC body phantom · Discovery MI
items.name: Small-sphere recovery and background noise
items.lede: The NEMA IEC body phantom with micro-spheres was simulated frame by frame, following the physical timing and F-18 decay, and compared with experimental Discovery MI scans in the same planes and on the same display scale.

fig.caption: Rows: contrasts 8:1 to 2:1. Columns: activity truth, experimental DMI image, CASSOULET simulation.

more: Recovery follows the experimental trend with sphere size; background noise is in the same range and slightly higher in simulation.
Reconstruction settings are on CASSOULET's internal β scale, not GE Q.Clear; several results are single noise realisations.

figs.caption: Recovery against sphere diameter, simulation vs experiment, per contrast.
Background coefficient of variation per contrast, experiment vs CASSOULET.

simulation.title: Case studies: simulation and models
simulation.lede: Studies that use the known truth directly: lesions in the abdominal phantom, reconstruction settings and the scanner models themselves.

items.name: Eleven synthetic lesions, OSEM vs BSREM
items.lede: Liver, lung and retroperitoneal lesions were inserted into the abdominal phantom: spheres from 6 to 20 mm plus a necrotic ring, a spiculated nodule, matted nodes and a satellite cluster. Each was reconstructed with OSEM and BSREM and scored against its truth.

fig.caption: Coronal MIP of the simulated abdominal phantom: activity truth, OSEM and BSREM.

more: Organ metrics (recovery, variability, NRMSE, bias) are reported per organ for both reconstructions.
Lesion cards show truth, OSEM and BSREM side by side with profiles and contrast recovery.
Dynamic FDG frames and a vessel-transit surrogate were also simulated; these are exploratory, not validated circulation.

figs.caption: Lesion L8: a 21 mm necrotic-ring liver lesion, truth vs reconstructions with a central profile.
Whole-VOI metrics by organ: OSEM vs BSREM.
Synthetic dynamic FDG PET of the phantom across the examination.

items.name: FDG from first pass to one hour

gsr.goal: See whether time-varying uptake survives simulation and reconstruction.
gsr.simulated: Organ uptake matched to a measured dynamic scan at 26–28 s, 5–6 min and 60–65 min, on an extended-length research scanner model.
gsr.results: Heart and kidney recovery 93–103 % across frames (median 101 %). Research geometry, not a commercial scanner.

fig.caption: Measured PET, matched input and simulation at three time points.

items.name: Choosing the Omni reconstruction strength

gsr.goal: Pick an internal β for the Omni model that behaves like the clinical Q.Clear setting.
gsr.simulated: The 36-insert cube on the Omni model, reconstructed at four β values from the same noisy data.
gsr.results: β 17.5 gave recovery 0.85 / 0.78 / 0.64 for 20 / 15 / 10 mm inserts and 3.7 % background noise; adopted as the Q.Clear 350 operating point for this protocol.

more: A protocol-specific choice, not a general vendor β conversion.

items.name: Simulated CT for attenuation and display

gsr.goal: Make a CT that both looks clinical and gives the right attenuation for PET.
gsr.simulated: A polychromatic 120 kVp fan-beam CT of the abdominal phantom with bowtie, quantum and electronic noise, FBP plus iterative refinement.
gsr.results: Organ CT numbers within 2.3 HU of the assigned reference (median 0.6 HU) across 16 regions on three slices. Some streaks remain.

fig.caption: Reference, clinical patient CT and simulated CT on matched slices.

items.name: Simulation-ready patients, built by AI agents with human review

gsr.goal: Turn routine PET/CT into simulation-ready patient models without losing control of quality.
gsr.simulated: AI segmentation (TotalSegmentator, MONAI, MOOSE), human correction queries, PET hot-spot extraction and organ uptake, applied by agents and reviewed by a human.
gsr.results: 10 patient models built: 7 accepted, 3 awaiting review, one case set aside. Simulations on both scanner models are next.

more: Patient images are not shown here.

items.name: OSEM, BSREM and Q.Clear-style settings
items.lede: Reconstruction choices change what a tool sees. CASSOULET reconstructs the same simulated data with different strategies and compares them with the ground truth and the physical console image.
more: β values are on CASSOULET's internal scale, not GE Q.Clear: an equivalent value has to be found by a sweep for each scanner and count level.
A ring/edge artefact in early runs was removed with a Tukey taper and a safe preconditioner.

items.name: Audits of the Discovery MI and Omni models
items.lede: The scanner models are audited like any other result: geometry against publications, count rates against published NEMA curves, and scatter against an independent Monte Carlo code.
more: Count calibration to published NEMA curves (DMI 20.84 cps/kBq, Omni 47.30 cps/kBq): withheld points reproduced within 1.1 / 1.0 / 3.9 % (DMI trues / scatter / randoms) and 0.7 / 1.0 / 0.5 % (Omni).
Scatter fraction in a 20 cm water cylinder: 27.1 % vs 28.0 % from SimSET, an independent code, with no tuning to that target.
Omni gap audit: no public block-gap dimensions were found, so the model states its packing assumptions instead of copying Discovery MI values.
These are research checks against published data, not vendor validation.

timeline.title: How CASSOULET grew
timeline.lede: From a MATLAB proof of concept to a 3D, GPU-based Python platform. Dates come from the project files; approximate ones are marked.

items.name: 2D analytical simulator in MATLAB
items.text: Command-line simulator on a PETSTEP-style architecture: 2D Radon projection, approximate corrections, 2.5D OSEM and a generic scanner, about 2–3 minutes per benchmark. Used for the PhD lesion-insertion and printed-phantom studies.

img.caption: MATLAB case study: lesion models to STL and masks, synthetic insertion in sinograms, and matching 3D-printed inserts.

items.name: CASSOULET V1 desktop GUI (MATLAB)
items.text: A launcher with shared lesion and STL workspaces: lesion editor, image-domain insertion, STL browser, printable insert modeller with gyroid lattices and an STL-to-mask voxelizer.

more.caption: STL modeller: primitives, boolean operations and gyroid meshing for printable inserts.
Lesion editor: modifier and designer tools with orthogonal and 3D views.
Lesion insertion workbench on a phantom image.
STL-to-mask voxelizer: masks generated from an STL surface.

items.name: MuPET preprint
items.text: Multiphysics PET: mass-transport physics with image-domain noise modelling, a fast image-level route that later joined CASSOULET as a module.

items.name: Python rebuild begins
items.text: A clean rebuild rather than a line-by-line port: a written blueprint, a PySide6 desktop shell with session folders, and a projection lab with scanner presets.

items.name: Desktop app alpha: four modules, one session
items.text: Designer workbench and mask editor, modeller, simulator and session map. The simulator switches between fast 2D Radon tests and 3D projection with parallelproj and PyTomography.

img.caption: Session map linking Design, Modeller, Simulation and Analysis.

items.name: 3D physics on GPU and scanner models
items.text: CASSOULET physics v2: Discovery MI 5-ring polygon model with depth of interaction, TOF single scatter and BSREM on A100 GPUs; an Omni Legend 32 cm model; the abdominal phantom; a multicentre virtual testbench. More than 150 dated studies by the end of October 2026.

items.name: A shared library, then digital twins
items.text: One documented simulation and reconstruction library behind every study, then physics-informed AI digital twins.

phantoms.title: Phantoms
phantoms.lede: Every study starts from an object whose truth is known. VeriTomiX uses three kinds, from standard to anthropomorphic.

items.name: CASSOULET abdominal phantom
items.text: Organs, vessels, bones, muscle and skin rebuilt from a public abdominal CT dataset (CC BY 4.0, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17407158), then given synthetic activity. It is the phantom in the 3D view.

fig.caption: Assembled anatomy, organs in position, bones and muscles.

figs.caption: Arteries, veins and predicted hepatic vessels.

items.name: NEMA IEC body phantom
items.text: The standard image-quality phantom, rebuilt as a CASSOULET template: D-shaped tank, lung insert and six micro-spheres from 4 to 12.4 mm, with PET activity, synthetic CT and a 511 keV μ-map.

fig.caption: NEMA IEC template viewer: PET activity, synthetic CT and μ-map.

items.name: 36-insert printed phantom
items.text: Porous 3D-printed cubes whose solidity sets the PET contrast, printed independently at two facilities from shared files and used as a common physical reference for the digital twins.

fig.caption: A common reference for multicentre PET: shared phantom geometry, independent experiments, matched assessment.
